title: Cricket API
description: Private monitoring of the Cricket API. Read-only, provisioned from the repository.

panels.title: API
panels.description: 1 when Prometheus can scrape the API's metrics listener, 0 when it cannot, no data when there is no target.

panels.title: Alerts
panels.description: Alerts that are firing now. The table at the bottom of the page lists them.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Latency, 95th percentile: the slowest 5 percent of requests took at least this long, over the last 5 minutes. Estimated from the histogram buckets. With no requests it is undefined and shows no data.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Requests a second that reached the origin, over the last 5 minutes. Cloudflare cache hits never get here.

panels.title: Refused
panels.description: Refused a second. Requests turned away: admission refusals (a class was full) plus per-client rate limit refusals (429).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Memory in use: the API process's memory as a share of its container limit. Page cache is left out because the kernel can reclaim it.

panels.title: Alerts firing now
panels.description: Every alert that is firing now, from Prometheus.

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: Business requests a second (the /v1 routes, health and status probes left out) that reached the origin. Cloudflare cache hits never get here, so this is not the traffic the site sees.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Business requests only (health probes left out so they do not pull the percentiles down). Estimated from the histogram buckets, so a value is only as precise as the bucket it falls in. With no requests the latency is undefined and the line is absent, not 0.

panels.title: Admission: refusals and waiting, by class
panels.description: Refusals a second (rooms full, wait ran out, a second heavy request from one client), and how many are waiting or running now, for each of the light, medium and heavy classes.

panels.title: Rate-limited (429) and faults
panels.description: Per-client rate limit refusals, unexpected faults (each is also in the fault log), queries stopped by the time limit, and queries refused because every slot stayed taken.

panels.title: API container memory against its limit
panels.description: Container memory includes page cache, which the kernel can reclaim, so compare it with the process resident line before acting on a high value.

panels.title: API CPU
panels.description: CPU the container used, and time it was held back by a CPU limit (the host has 2 vCPUs).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the API process started. A short value means a recent restart.

panels.title: Data age
panels.description: Time since the served files were built. The alert threshold is provisional.

panels.title: Data version
panels.description: The data version of the files being served.

panels.title: Disk used, by filesystem
panels.description: Percent used. The host disk's alert lines are at 55, 70 and 85. A fixed-size volume that fills stops its owner and nothing else.

panels.title: Free space, inodes and forecast
panels.description: Free bytes on the host disk and where the last 6 and 24 hours' trend would take them. A line below zero is the alert condition.

targets.legendFormat: free in 24 h at the 6 h rate
free in 7 d at the 24 h rate

panels.title: Inodes
panels.description: Percent of inodes used on the host disk. Alert at 80.

panels.title: Growth, 7 d
panels.description: How much more of the host disk is used than 7 days ago. Needs 7 days of data.

panels.title: Journal
panels.description: System journal size, from the disk scan. Limit 400 MB.

panels.title: Images
panels.description: Docker image size, from the disk scan. Budget 4 GB.

panels.title: Prometheus
panels.description: Prometheus's own data against its 1.5 GB limit (on a 2 GB volume).

panels.title: Scan age
panels.description: Time since the disk scan last wrote its metrics. Alert at 30 minutes. No data means it has never run.

panels.title: Each part against its budget
panels.description: Each component's size as a share of its row in the disk budget. Over 1 (100 percent) for an hour is an alert. A component with no scan data is missing, not 0.

panels.title: Outbound traffic this month (500 GB allowance)
panels.description: At least this share of the 500 GB monthly allowance, from the notifier's hourly record of the public interface (UTC calendar month). It includes SSH, updates and mail calls, and may not match how OVH counts.

panels.title: Traffic this month, and hours not measured
panels.description: Bytes counted so far this month, and the whole hours that the notifier could not measure. A month figure with unmeasured hours is 'at least'.

panels.title: Outbound rate on the public interface
panels.description: Transmit rate by interface. The notifier's configured bandwidth device is the public one.

panels.title: Messages by state
panels.description: Messages in the ledger by state. 'accepted' means Resend returned a message id: delivery is not tracked.

panels.title: Send budgets used
panels.description: What the notifier has charged in the current UTC day and month, as a share of what each class may use. Summaries have a reserve, and the suppression, email-path and host notices the last slots.

panels.title: Account usage reported by Resend
panels.description: What Resend last reported for the whole account in the current UTC day and month (the free plan allows 100 a day and 3,000 a month). The gap from the notifier's own use is mail from somewhere else. No data when none is known for the period.

panels.title: Failed or unconfirmed
panels.description: Messages that failed or are unconfirmed and not yet reviewed.

panels.title: Summary overdue
panels.description: How far past its grace period a due summary is. Zero when none is due.

panels.title: Oldest past its deadline
panels.description: How far the most overdue unsent message is past its deadline.

panels.title: Time since the last accepted message
panels.description: For information only, not an alert: a quiet day has just the daily summary, so a day of silence is normal. No data when nothing is in the ledger.

panels.title: Circuit breaker
panels.description: Closed is normal. Open means sending failed three times in a row and alert mail is being held.

panels.title: Ledger storage
panels.description: The ledger's storage guard. Anything but ok means alert webhooks may be refused (Alertmanager retries).
